protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: Confirmed. The decoder recursively follows each compression pointer, while seen_pointers only rejects repeated offsets and MAX_DNS_LABELS only checks accumulated labels after recursion. A chain of unique forward pointers can therefore exceed Python's recursion limit without either guard firing, and pre-fix DECODE_EXCEPTIONS omits RecursionError.
protocol_checks.atomic_bic: Confirmed as 0a36cc6815a7c6593b249242a6854e1a7ca3b590. It is the first reconstructable PR #934 member and first writes _decode_labels_at_offset plus the unbounded recursive call; later 15a89a0ed8b9ba61814ba15d0b573c556cbc44c5 only moves the same mechanism into DNSIncoming.
protocol_checks.immediate_parent_absence: Confirmed against 4d30c25fe57425bcae36a539006e44941ef46e2c. The parent has none of _decode_labels_at_offset, DnsNameReader, MAX_DNS_LABELS, or DECODE_EXCEPTIONS and uses an iterative read_name loop that rejects forward pointers with off >= first, so the vulnerable recursive mechanism is absent.
